title: Development Costs
author: Legitimate_Bank_6573
selftext:
Hey everyone, aspiring AI developer here. Got an idea, no one else has made it, I'd like to.

I've already started with GPT6 and Codex and we've got a solid foundation, obvious room for improvement and there's a lot of information I don't have.

My number one question for people with more information who've been doing this longer than me, how much are you spending on development? I see a lot of people with a lot of suggestions for workflows but no one's really elaborating on how much they're costing you to use.

Currently I'm only in the cost of GPTPro, I'm wondering how much my budget of "as free as humanely possible" is holding me back.

comments.author: Masterkiefs
comments.body:
Give Opus 5.5 a shot, I think you may enjoy it a lot in your workflow. Opus 5.5 can build as usage an output is great. Have the cheaper plan for codex and have it audit your work as needed.   
  
In terms of cost, Its primary depends on your project, the style of game, etc. A lot can be done with just your claude/codex subscription. 

Blender = free  
Fab = lots of free assets  
unity = also has free assets.

There are available commercial sounds for free you can use.

At this point of day, the cost is one of the cheapest for indie developers to start, as the barriers to entry are reduced with AI.

comments.author: According-Pressure39
comments.body: How many Tokens with Pro? I can Tell you, if you have a Plan and a Vision, keep holding on to it, finish the Game and Release it ONLY in a good State!

replies.author: je386
replies.body:
Claude is great. I mostly use claude haiku through github copilot coding agent. Haiku 5.5 is more than capable for tasks where I used claude sonnet 4.5 before.  
And haiku only needs 1-10% of the tokens sonnet wants.

replies.author: Templeshooter
replies.body: there is nothing wrong, I use claude code, but my colleagues who use codex told me it's good as well

replies.author: Charming_You_25
replies.body:
Gpt was better value up until opus 5.5 came out. Now it’s slower and more expensive. Astra has marginally better output than opus 5.5 but fable is better still. Also there’s a consistency difference. Gpt is all over the place doing dumb things and really smart things. Opus and fable you can trust will perform at a certain level.

My budget seems way higher than most ppl here (I have 3 200 subs. 2 Claude and 1 gpt). I am now reaching for fable most of the time though Astra is still the best at hammering at a problem. Claude gives a good answer quickly but Astra finds more edge cases.

Gpt is still decent value if you’re using the resets and are ok with sitting on your hands the weeks they don’t have them. But I can’t work with that inconsistency

comments.author: Felmeric
comments.body: I'm spending about 40$ a month. 20 on claude code, 20 on gamelabs for easy to use art. I'm more of a hobbyists so this might not be that helpful if you are aiming to sell your game.

comments.author: Empuda
comments.body: Depends on you and your project needs. Making something simple == less money. Making something faster == more money. Making something complex and fast == 2nd mortgage.

replies.author: Empuda
replies.body: 3rd mortgage it is :) You decide what engine? 2d? 3d? What other arps inspire you?
